records.name: Civil Rights Act of 1964
records.goal: Prohibit discrimination in public accommodations and employment; strengthen voting and civil rights protection.
proArguments: Equal access and dignity; racial discrimination was a national problem requiring federal action.
conArguments: Opponents invoked constitutional limits on federal power and argued existing statutes sufficed; segregationist opponents also sought to preserve racial separation.
amendments: Mansfield–Dirksen substitute offered May 26; adopted June 17 (76–18). Individual amendment details unverified.
records.notes: Historical arguments are attributed, not endorsed. Final outcomes only in audit.

records.name: Voting Rights Act of 1965
records.bill: H.R. 6400 (House measure); Senate bill number unverified
records.goal: Counter discriminatory voter registration; federal examiners and preclearance in covered jurisdictions.
proArguments: Federal protection was necessary because state and local registration practices excluded eligible voters.
conArguments: Specific congressional opponents and arguments require further review; do not infer from modern party alignment.

records.name: Gulf of Tonkin Resolution
records.goal: Authorize presidential military action in Southeast Asia.
proArguments: Administration sought congressional support for action against reported attacks.
conArguments: Congressional war powers and scope of authorization were disputed.
records.notes: Additional bill-level metadata not independently verified.

records.name: Equal Rights Amendment
records.sponsor: Martha Griffiths championed House measure; Birch Bayh managed Senate measure; formal sponsor metadata pending
records.goal: Constitutional guarantee of equality of legal rights regardless of sex.
proArguments: Existing state and judicial remedies did not eliminate persistent sex discrimination.
conArguments: Ervin raised federalism, military-service and protective labor law concerns.
amendments: House version substituted in Senate; Ervin amendments rejected; individual amendment texts not verified.
records.outcome: Congress proposed the amendment; state ratification separate, not implied by this vote.

records.name: Reorganization Plan No. 3 of 1970
opponents: John Dingell (D-MI) proposed a broader alternative
proArguments: Coordinate pollution control and research across agencies.
conArguments: Dingell argued that a larger cabinet-level department could cover omitted programs.

records.name: Title IX of the Education Amendments of 1972
records.goal: Prohibit sex discrimination in federally assisted educational programs.
proArguments: Equal educational opportunity regardless of sex.
records.notes: Opposition and formal bill information unverified.

records.name: War Powers Resolution
records.goal: Reassert Congress's constitutional role in decisions regarding military hostilities; reporting and time limits.
proArguments: Congress should exercise its constitutional responsibilities over war and peace; Vietnam underscored the need to limit unilateral presidential action.
conArguments: Nixon objected on constitutional and security grounds. Elizabeth Holtzman (D-NY) criticized the measure from the opposite direction, as too permissive of presidential action.

records.name: Congressional Budget and Impoundment Control Act of 1974
records.goal: Strengthen congressional budget coordination and fiscal authority relative to the executive.
proArguments: Reassert congressional power of the purse and rebalance executive-legislative power.

records.name: Torrijos–Carter Treaties
records.goal: Protect long-term access to canal while transferring control to Panama.
proArguments: Secure canal access and improve relations with Latin American countries.
conArguments: Conservative opponents argued transfer posed a strategic threat and distrusted Torrijos.
stages: Senate consent to Panama Canal Treaty, 68–32

records.name: National Energy Act package
records.goal: Conservation, energy taxation and natural gas policy reforms.

records.name: Economic Opportunity Act of 1964
records.goal: Expand access to employment, training and community anti-poverty programs.
proArguments: Johnson argued that opportunity and job training could address causes of poverty rather than relying solely on relief.
records.notes: Presidential signing remarks confirm date and policy rationale; opposition and legislative metadata pending.

records.name: Immigration and Nationality Act Amendments of 1965
records.goal: Replace national-origins quota system with new immigration preferences.
proArguments: Johnson argued that origin-based quotas violated principles of equal treatment.
